The location and effluent volume of the proposed facility to handle domestic wastes during construction are not known at this time. When this dama becomes available, the applicant will inform the FPC staff.

3.2.1.1 Scenic and Esthetic Resources
Page 3-15
Paragraph two - the maximum drawdown of 160 feet will not be a "normal" feature. Only in a week during summer peak load, a maximum drawdown up to elevation 2160 can be expected. The phrase "normal minimum pool elevation" is misleading. Horever the "mudflat" will be visible from the air and from certain specific locations.
Section 3.2.1 has been revised to clarify this point.
Paragraph three refers to submerged tree stumps. These will be removed during clearing in borrow areas.
Section 3.2.1 has been revised.
3.2.1.2 Recreation
Page 3-17
Paragraph two - The design of the proposed shelters has not been finally determined by Duke. The shelter described in Exhibit R-2 is designed to accommodate six persons and their gear, however Duke may elect to modify the size of a shelter to suit its location.
Section 3.2.1.2 has been revised.
The statement recommends that the shelters should be spaced equidistant along the trail. Duke contends that the shelter locacion should be determined by the difficulty of the trail and availability of suitable sites.
Staff concurs. Section 3.2.1.2 has been revised.
3.2.4.2 Water Quality
Page 3-27
The first paragraph makes reference to a multi-level outlet structure for minimum flows into Howard Creek. The intake levels in Bad Creek Reservoir for the Howard Creek flow augmentation pipe will be at elevations 2280 ft., 2230 ft., and 2120 ft. These openings are 30 ft., 80 ft., and 190 ft. below full pool elevation, and will allow water of various temperatures and D. O. concentration to be used for flow augmentation. See Exhibit W, Figure 1.4-4, Amendment 1.
Section 3.2.2.2 has been revised to include this information.
